title: fix(ui): the state-machine chip shows its grey dot when an option has no colour; the triplet-token scan covers every theme token
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuVwX4pUdM1qvNLSqRZNSvv3)_

Fixes #35962
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none

## 维护者速读

- 元数据查看器的「状态机」面板里，没有设置颜色的状态，标签前的小圆点在浅色和深色主题下都恢复显示为灰色（之前是一块空白）。
- 来自「列表页重做」专题里危险红色修复时发现的同类问题，并把那次加的颜色写法检查从红色扩展到主题里所有同类颜色。
- 出错最坏是某个状态圆点的颜色和以前不同；只改显示，不动数据，可以直接撤回。
- 无

## What changes

- **The fallback dot.** The state-machine chip in the metadata viewer painted its dot with an inline `backgroundColor: color ?? 'var(--muted-foreground)'`. `--muted-foreground` holds a bare HSL triplet (`215.4 16.3% 46.9%`), so with no option colour the declaration was dropped and the dot rendered transparent. The card proposed wrapping the fallback in `hsl()`. That fixes the colour, but leaves a component-chosen colour written inline as `backgroundColor`, which `ui/AGENTS.md` (Tech Stack, Styling) forbids, and the author's option colour on the same line breaks the same rule. So the dot now follows the one permitted shape from `skills/objectui/rules/styling.md` ("Author-Declared, Data-Driven Colour"):
  - no option colour: the `bg-muted-foreground` utility, which resolves through the theme in light and `.dark`;
  - a declared option colour: published as the custom property `--os-state-dot` and painted by the static utility `bg-[color:var(--os-state-dot)]`.
  The dot gains a `data-state-dot` attribute naming its state value, so the test can find it.
- **The scan, widened.** The source scan from the danger-colour fix (`destructive-colour-spelling-35911.test.ts`) used to look only for bare `var(--destructive…)`. It now reads the token list from the theme blocks: every `:root` and `.dark` block in the components, Console and runner stylesheets and in the CLI app generator's template. Every custom property stored there as a bare triplet counts, plus the engine variable a triplet token reads with a triplet fallback (`--destructive-text-light` / `-dark`). That makes 44 tokens on this tree, none of them typed in the test. A `var()` of any of those tokens fails the scan unless it sits directly inside `hsl()`/`hsla()`, is the value of a custom property (a triplet aliasing a triplet), or is the fallback of an outer `var()` that is itself in one of those positions. Tailwind 4's `bg-(--token)` shorthand compiles to the same bare `var()` and is scanned too. The existing destructive cases are kept: the destructive tokens are asserted to be in the derived list, and the fill/stroke and Markdown-theme cases are unchanged.
- **What the widened scan found.** Two hits on the base tree: the chip above, and a usage example in a comment in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/styles.css` (the shimmer utility's doc comment), which suggested `var(--muted)` / `var(--muted-foreground)/10` inside a gradient. The comment now spells them `hsl(var(--muted))` / `hsl(var(--muted-foreground)/0.1)`. It is a comment only, so it ships nothing and has zero consumers (a grep for `linear-gradient(90deg,var(--muted)` and for `animate-shimmer` users finds only the comment), but the next author would copy it. No other same-family misspelling exists under `ui/packages/*/src` or `ui/apps/*/src`.

## Tests

- `metadata-viewer.test.tsx`: new case "paints a state dot from the theme grey when its option has no colour, and from the declared colour otherwise". The no-colour dot carries `bg-muted-foreground` and no inline style. The coloured dot carries the custom property and no inline `backgroundColor`.
- `destructive-colour-spelling-35911.test.ts`: three new cases. (1) The token list is read from every theme file, each contributing at least two blocks and more than 20 triplets, and it holds the destructive family, `--muted-foreground`, `--border` and `--chart-1`, but not `--surface`, `--text-muted`, `--radius` or `--shadow-sm`. (2) Detector fixtures, bare vs wrapped. (3) The widened bare-read scan.

## Acceptance notes

- **Mechanism changed against the card's suggested route, intent kept.** The card says "wrap"; this PR uses the utility plus custom-property shape because the inline-colour ban in `ui/AGENTS.md` binds. Both spellings render the same grey (browser reading below), and the ablation reintroduces the original bare spelling.
- The author's declared colour still paints the same in light and dark, as before. A dark-adjusted variant, like the one the fields badge derives, is not in scope here.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:
1. `ui/packages/components/src/__tests__/destructive-colour-spelling-35911.test.ts`: the `themeBlocks` / `tripletTokens` reader and the `wrapped` predicate. The risk is a false negative, so read how the fallback recursion decides.
2. `ui/packages/components/src/renderers/basic/metadata-viewer.tsx`: the `Chip` dot.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/components/src/__tests__/destructive-colour-spelling-35911.test.ts packages/components/src/__tests__/metadata-viewer.test.tsx`. Expected: 2 files and 15 tests pass.

<details><summary>Ablation: reintroduce the bare spelling, and the scan goes red</summary>

Run through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, with the anchor on the new `style=` line and the replacement `style={{ backgroundColor: color ?? 'var(--muted-foreground)' }}`:

```
ablation-replace: ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob 56997c92f6de -> 523ec6d0c861
     × no shipped source uses a bare var() of a triplet theme token as a colour value
+   "packages/components/src/renderers/basic/metadata-viewer.tsx:296: style={{ backgroundColor: color ?? 'var(--muted-foreground)' }}",
 Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
ablation-replace: ok restored: blob == HEAD (56997c92f6de) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```
The scan reads source from disk, so no build is involved.
</details>

<details><summary>Browser reading (Chromium, built components stylesheet, light and .dark)</summary>

Computed `background-color` of four dots rendered against `ui/packages/components/dist/index.css` after `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components build`, which emits both `.bg-muted-foreground` and `.bg-[color:var(--os-state-dot)]`:

```
light {"fallback":"rgb(100, 116, 139)","declared":"rgb(16, 185, 129)","old":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","cardwrap":"rgb(100, 116, 139)"}
dark  {"fallback":"rgb(148, 163, 184)","declared":"rgb(16, 185, 129)","old":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","cardwrap":"rgb(148, 163, 184)"}
```
`old` is the base tree's spelling (transparent, the defect). `fallback` is this PR's dot. `cardwrap` is the card's `hsl()` wrap, which renders the same grey.
</details>

<details><summary>Local gates</summary>

All readings were taken on head `bca3f7d1`.

- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/components^...' --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` (the dependency closure): VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check` (tsc over `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.test.json`; `--listFilesOnly` shows both touched test files are compiled): exit 0.
- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/components/`: 497 test files passed and 1 skipped; 4772 tests passed and 24 skipped; VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 38 families from this diff. All 38 exited 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reports 38 derived, 38 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN, and "a DERIVED zero".
- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run scripts/` (one of the 38): 172 test files passed. On the first head it was red, because `check-hand-rolled-comment-mask` flagged the scan's private comment regex. The block reader now uses `maskComments` from `ui/scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`, and it is green.
- The full UI test, the type-check lanes and the remaining CI families are left to CI.
</details>
